source.title: The Differentiable Cross-Entropy Method
source.venue: ICML 2020 (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, vol. 119)

confidence_rationale: This is the canonical, peer-reviewed (ICML 2020) precedent for exactly SD-055's design move: replacing CEM's non-differentiable top-k / argsort elite-selection step with a temperature-controlled soft aggregate so gradients flow back through candidate selection to upstream parameters, and applying it to continuous control / planning. SD-055's softmax-weighted candidate mean (with temperature T) is a specific instance of DCEM's smooth top-k. High confidence: the mapping is structural and direct, the venue is strong, and the method is exactly the one SD-055 implements. Held below 0.9 because DCEM uses a more general smooth top-k (LML projection) whereas SD-055 uses the simplest softmax-mean special case, so DCEM validates the family but not the specific tightness of SD-055's approximation.
failure_signatures: If the soft-selection gradient were shown to be too biased/high-variance to improve learning over the non-differentiable baseline, it would weaken SD-055's premise that restoring gradient to cue_action_proj is beneficial.

DCEM still relies on the objective being meaningfully differentiable w.r.t. the candidates; if SD-055's score->action_bias path through E2 rollouts has near-zero usable gradient, the differentiable selection would restore a path that carries no signal.
DCEM reports the soft relaxation helps in some control settings but is not uniformly better than vanilla CEM; a null or negative result in REE would be consistent with that variance.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The cross-entropy method's elite-selection step (hard top-k thresholding over candidate costs) is non-differentiable, which blocks end-to-end gradient-based learning of the objective's parameters. Replacing it with a temperature-scaled soft top-k operation makes the CEM output differentiable w.r.t. the objective parameters; as the temperature decreases the soft operation approaches the original hard selection. Applied to energy-based structured prediction and to fine-tuning CEM-based continuous controllers.
mapping.ree_translation: DCEM is the direct ML precedent for SD-055. HippocampalModule.propose_trajectories() uses torch.argsort() to rank candidates and indexes elites by rank -- a zero-gradient barrier that severs action_bias (from SD-016 cue_action_proj) from the task-reward signal. SD-055 replaces argsort + indexed elite-mean with softmax(-scores/T) weighting over all candidates, exactly the temperature-controlled soft elite-selection DCEM formalises. The temperature T plays DCEM's role: low T concentrates weight near argmax, high T averages broadly. DCEM establishes that this move restores gradient to upstream parameters and is usable for planning/control.
mapping.mapping_caveat: DCEM's soft top-k is the more general Limited-Multi-Label (LML) projection; SD-055 uses the simplest softmax-weighted mean over ALL candidates (the T-controlled top-1-style aggregate), which is a looser approximation of true elite selection. So DCEM supports the family and the rationale, but does not specifically validate that SD-055's dense softmax-mean preserves CEM's elite semantics tightly. DCEM also fine-tunes a controller; SD-055 keeps ARC-007's value-flat residue-terrain scoring (no new value head), so the objective being differentiated differs. The precedent is methodological, not a same-task result.
mapping.source_context: Machine-learning methods paper (ICML 2020) on making CEM differentiable for end-to-end learning, with continuous-control / model-based RL experiments; reference implementation at github.com/facebookresearch/dcem.

confidence_components.notes: Strong venue (ICML), directly on-point method. Mapping fidelity high because SD-055 is essentially a special case of this method applied to the same class of operation (CEM elite selection in a planner). Transfer risk low -- this is ML->ML, same problem class; the only gap is general smooth top-k vs SD-055's softmax-mean special case.
